To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there is limited evidence that engaging in agriculture is associated with lower incidence and/or prevalence of CVDs, and lower prevalence of CVD risk factors, compared with non-agrarian employment, in LMICs.

there is limited evidence of varying consistency that rural agricultural workers have a lower prevalence of CVD risk factors, including hypertension, overweight/obesity and smoking, and a higher prevalence in underweight, compared with non-agrarian workers.
there is limited evidence of varying consistency on the association of engaging and transitioning out of agricultural employment with CVDs and risk factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association of engaging or not engaging in agriculture with atherosclerosis and its risk factors.
the health effects of labour-force transitions in LMICs, particularly those related to agriculture.
the health of rural workers and the health of the population in rural areas in low- and lower-middle-income countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
agricultural engagement is associated with lower CVD incidence or prevalence and CVD risk factor prevalence in LMICs, but there is a need for further high quality research.
agricultural engagement is associated with lower incidence and prevalence of atherosclerortic cardiovascular diseases and cardiovascular risk factors in low- and medium-income countries.
the available evidence is too limited to support or refute the hypothesis that agricultural engagement is associated with lower prevalence of CVDs and cardiovascular risk factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
agricultural engagement may be associated with lower prevalence of CVD risk factors.
agricultural engagement is not necessarily associated with lower CVD incidence and CVD risk factor prevalence in LMICs, but that the quality of evidence for this conclusion is limited.
the evidence is limited and inconsistent, but suggests that engaging in agriculture is associated with lower incidence and prevalence of CVDs and risk factors in LMICS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the association between engaging in agriculture compared with non-agriultural employment and cardiovascular disease incidence, prevalence and cardiovascular disease risk factor prevalence in LMICs is unclear.
there is a lack of studies on the effect that engaging in agriculture has on atheroscleretic cardiovascular disease (CVD) and CVD risk factor prevalence in low- and medium-income countries (LMICS).
there are no studies that assess the association of agriculture engagement and CVD incidence or prevalence.
